transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello! I'm Dora, and I'm here to help with any questions you may have about your cataract surgery recovery. How are you feeling after your surgery? Do you have any questions about your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi, Dora! Thanks for calling. I'm doing pretty well, but I do have a few questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You can start light exercise, like gardening, about 1 week after surgery. However, it's best to avoid heavy lifting, bending, or strenuous activity for a month. Just be sure to wear protective eyewear when you're gardening, especially if you're doing anything that might get debris in your eyes.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Okay, that makes sense. Thank you! My next question is, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You can start using your preservative-free eye drops as soon as you need them, not necessarily a specific time after surgery. You were prescribed to use them four times daily to start, and you can get more from your GP if you're running out.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Got it, thanks! I have another question: I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended: It's normal to be a bit sensitive to light as your eyes adjust to the new lenses. If it's mild and you just feel like things are a bit brighter than usual, wearing sunglasses outside might help. But if you're experiencing significant pain or discomfort when it's bright, we may need to check it further.
transcript.delivered: It's normal to be a bit sensitive to light as your eyes adjust to the new lenses.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Do you have any other questions about your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, one more question: should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: It's common to have blurry vision in the first week after surgery, but it should improve quickly and settle down over time. If your vision is still blurry or getting worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything is okay.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Okay, thank you for the information. That's really helpful! I don't have any more questions right now. Thanks so much for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're welcome! I'm glad I could help. I want to make sure you feel confident about your recovery. Before we go, can you confirm that all your questions have been answered?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, all my questions have been answered. Thanks again for your assistance!
